$comment: Five production machines from Arffornia/docs specs 002 and 003 (P3), each with its marks (the machine at a later tier) and four design variations. A prompt = machine.core + mark.text + lineage + variation + footprint + brief. Footprints are W x D x H in blocks (spec 002, before decision DA2 on scale). Lineage (P4, Brian: 'pas forcé sur toutes les machines d'avoir un pattern qui s'améliore, il faut que ce soit cohérent'): each machine says how its tiers relate. mode 'evolves': every later mark keeps the Mk1 chassis (chassis 'shared', with 'keeps'). mode 'branches': some later mark is a new design (chassis 'new', with 'why'). mode 'single': one mark only, for machines with no believable primitive tier (a particle accelerator). Shared marks reuse the Mk1 seeds, so a variation's marks start from the same composition.

smelter.title: Smelter
smelter.core: A compact ore smelter: crushed ore goes in at the top, glowing ingots come out of a pour spout into an ingot mould line at the front. Square footprint, squat and heavy, about three metres tall.

lineage.why: All three are crucible furnaces; only the heat source changes, like Satisfactory's Miner Mk1-3.

mk1.text: Mark 1, coal-fired: a cast-iron firebox door at the bottom with flames visible through the vents, a small coal hopper and a short riveted chimney with a spark guard.

mk2.text: Mark 2, electric induction: the firebox is replaced by thick copper induction coils wrapped around the crucible, a cable conduit and a transformer box bolted to the side; no chimney, a fume extraction duct instead.
mk2.keeps: the square steel frame, the crucible, the pour spout and the ingot mould line

mk3.text: Mark 3, plasma arc: a plasma torch head on an articulated mount points down into the crucible, with magnetic field rings around the hearth and heavy shielding plates.
mk3.keeps: the square steel frame, the crucible, the pour spout and the ingot mould line

variations.v1: Round crucible furnace inside a square steel frame, ore fed by a small bucket elevator on the side.
variations.v2: Square shaft furnace with a skip hoist that tips ore into the top, pour spout on a short launder.
variations.v3: Two small crucibles side by side on a shared base, each tilting on trunnions to pour.
variations.v4: Low horizontal rotary kiln tube on rollers driven by a gear ring, discharging at one end.

constructor.title: Constructor
constructor.core: A forming machine that turns one ingot into one part (plates, rods, screws): a press station on a long narrow base, raw ingots enter on a short conveyor at one end and finished parts drop into a chute at the other end. Rectangular footprint, longer than wide.

lineage.why: A press stays a press: the frame and the flow stay, the drive goes steam, hydraulic, servo.

mk1.text: Mark 1, steam: a heavy drop hammer driven by a large flywheel and a flat drive belt from a small coal-fired steam engine with a piston and crank at the back.

mk2.text: Mark 2, electric hydraulic: the steam engine is replaced by an electric motor driving a hydraulic pump, the hammer becomes a hydraulic press with two guide columns and visible hoses.
mk2.keeps: the long narrow base, the input conveyor, the output chute and the press frame

mk3.text: Mark 3, servo forming cell: a multi-stage servo press with a transfer arm moving parts between three dies, a glass guard panel, cable chains.
mk3.keeps: the long narrow base, the input conveyor, the output chute and the press frame

variations.v1: C-frame press with the ram visible from the side, open front.
variations.v2: Four-column press with a moving platen and a die change cart parked beside it.
variations.v3: Roller mill: two big counter-rotating rolls flatten the ingot into a plate.
variations.v4: Rotary head that stamps, turns and cuts in sequence, with an indexing table.

assembler.title: Assembler
assembler.core: An assembly station that combines two input parts into one component: two input conveyors on the long sides, a work table in the middle, the finished component leaves on a conveyor at the end. Long rectangular footprint, three by five blocks.

lineage.why: Mechanical arms become robots on the same table; micro-assembly needs a sealed room, so Mk3 is a new machine.

mk1.text: Mark 1, mechanical: line shafts and cams drive two simple pick-and-place arms on real hinges, a rotating index table, everything powered by a belt from an overhead shaft.

mk2.text: Mark 2, electric robotics: two six-axis industrial robot arms on pedestals with cable dress packs, a welding torch on one arm, a gripper on the other, a safety fence around the cell.
mk2.keeps: the long work table, the two side input conveyors and the output conveyor

mk3.text: Mark 3, sealed micro-assembly: the open cell becomes a sealed cleanroom pod with small arms behind a glass window, an airlock on the input side and violet energy conduits.
mk3.why: a cleanroom pod has nothing in common with an open cell

variations.v1: Overhead gantry crane spanning the table, arms hanging from the gantry carriage.
variations.v2: Arms on floor pedestals facing each other across the table.
variations.v3: Linear line: three stations in a row along the long axis, each adding one step.
variations.v4: Turntable in the middle with four fixtures, arms around it.

foundry.title: Foundry
foundry.core: A large alloy foundry, the first flagship multiblock: two ores or ingots go in, molten alloy is poured from a big crucible into a casting line. Big square footprint, five blocks wide and tall, with a walkway around the top.

lineage.why: Coke and arc furnaces share a tilting body; a levitation crucible has no walls to share, so Mk3 is a new machine.

mk1.text: Mark 1, coke-fired: a brick-lined tilting crucible furnace with a coke hopper, a tall chimney stack with a damper, hot slag runner at the side.

mk2.text: Mark 2, electric arc furnace: three huge graphite electrodes on a hydraulic mast pass through a swinging roof, a transformer vault beside it, bus bars and water-cooled cables.
mk2.keeps: the furnace body on its trunnions, the casting line and the top walkway

mk3.text: Mark 3, levitation crucible: the molten alloy floats inside a ring of electromagnets, no crucible walls, violet-white plasma heating, heavy radiation shielding.
mk3.why: a field-held melt replaces the furnace itself

variations.v1: Furnace tilts on big trunnions driven by a hydraulic ram to pour into a ladle.
variations.v2: A bridge crane carries a ladle from the furnace to a row of moulds.
variations.v3: Two furnaces feed one mixing ladle in the middle, symmetrical layout.
variations.v4: Continuous casting: the alloy runs down a curved strand with rollers and comes out as bars.

refinery.title: Refinery
refinery.core: A fluid refinery: crude goes in by pipe on one face, fuel and plastic come out by pipe on the opposite face. A tall distillation column, a heater and heat exchangers on a long rectangular steel skid, five by seven blocks, seven tall.

lineage.why: Two marks on one skid; there is no believable plasma refinery, so it stops at Mk2.

mk1.text: Mark 1, fired heater: an oil-fired box heater with a small flare stack, the column has external ladders and platforms, valves and pressure gauges everywhere.

mk2.text: Mark 2, electric catalytic cracker: the heater becomes an electric reactor vessel with a catalyst hopper and a cyclone separator, teal status lights.
mk2.keeps: the steel skid, the distillation column and the pipe faces

variations.v1: One tall column with a spiral stair, the heater at its foot.
variations.v2: Two shorter columns side by side joined by a pipe bridge.
variations.v3: Horizontal layout: the column lies along the skid on saddles, with a pump station.
variations.v4: Column inside an open steel frame with three platform levels and a small crane on top.
